headline: California's governor has signed a large batch of AI and privacy bills, including one that bars employers from relying only on automated systems to fire or discipline staff.
score_reason: The signings ended on 30 Sep 2026, before the edition window; one point lower than the pool score.
importance_line: Workers, children and consumers in California get new protections and companies new duties, though lawyers expect disputes over broad definitions and some bills were vetoed.
summary: WilmerHale reports on JD Supra that after the legislature passed dozens of AI and privacy bills on 31 Aug 2026, Governor Gavin Newsom signed SB 947, the "No Robo Bosses Act of 2026", on 30 Sep, the signing deadline, and signed child online safety bills AB 226, AB 1709 and SB 1119, which include rules for chatbots used by minors, on 10 Sep. Law firm Wilson Sonsini counts more than two dozen such bills enacted, and the package also tightens data broker deletion rules.
notes: Original (Wilson Sonsini, wsgr.com) blocked with 403; credited WilmerHale's review of the same session instead. The 'over two dozen' count is Wilson Sonsini's headline only. Score 7 to 6.
